problem: writeExportFile swallows every mkdir/writeFile failure: the catch only logs, and only when KERYX_VERBOSE is set. Its sole caller, runHistoryExport (line 122), then goes on to print 'exported N run(s) to <file>' (line 131) and leaves exitCode at 0. That breaks error-handling.mdc Rule 3 and Iron Law 1. The class has one site: writeExportFile is the only write path in the new module.
impact: A user or script that exports to an unwritable path (read-only directory, EACCES, ENOSPC, a path whose parent is a file) is told the export succeeded and gets exit 0, then attaches or reads a file that does not exist. The fix is to let the error propagate, or rethrow it with a message naming the file and { cause }.

problem: The JSDoc on collectRunRows says it returns the runs oldest first. The function only filters the result of listWikiRuns, which is documented as 'Runs newest first' and sorts descending (src/wiki/history.ts:495-508). Nothing reverses the order, so the comment describes a behaviour that has no code path.
impact: The next reader or caller trusts the comment and believes the exported file is chronological. The wiki help text in the same change still says 'newest first'. Either the comment or the code has to change.

problem: The rethrow drops the original error: there is no { cause }, and the caught `error` is never used. The message does not say which runs log or which cwd failed. This goes against error-handling.mdc Rule 2, Rule 5 and Iron Law 3.
impact: Someone debugging a failed export sees a generic message with no errno, path or stack from listWikiRuns, so they cannot tell a missing log from a parse or permission failure.
quote: throw new Error("wiki history: could not read the runs log");

problem: The command-label sanitizer (collapse newlines, collapse whitespace, trim, slice to MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH) is copied three times in this change: wiki-history-export.ts:49-53 (markdown branch), wiki-history-export.ts:56-60 (CSV branch) and wiki-history.ts:47-51 (text listing). Only MAX_COMMAND_WIDTH is shared, not the transformation.
impact: Any change to how labels are cleaned or clipped has to be made in three places and kept in sync. The two copies inside renderRunLine are identical and sit only a few lines apart.

problem: renderRunLine takes four positional parameters, and the last one is a boolean flag (`markdown`) that switches between two different renderers. The call site reads `renderRunLine(run, at, run.pages, format === "md")`. `pages` repeats run.pages, and `at` is a normalization of run.at that the caller works out itself (line 118). Both are part of `run`, so the signature splits one value across three arguments. solid-principles.mdc thresholds: boolean flag that selects behaviour, and 4 or more positional parameters with no options object.
impact: Call sites cannot be read without the signature. A caller could pass a `pages` or `at` that disagrees with `run`. Adding a third format means growing the flag into a discriminant. Splitting it into renderCsvRow(run) and renderMarkdownRow(run), or keying a renderer by RunExportFormat, removes all three problems.

problem: runHistoryExport is about 57 lines long (75-132) and does separable jobs at different levels of abstraction: it parses and validates three options (--export, --format with extension inference, --since with a date-only regex), queries, normalizes timestamps inline (line 118), renders, writes the file, and resolves the path it displays. That passes the solid-principles.mdc length threshold with two separable jobs.
impact: Option parsing cannot be unit-tested apart from file I/O; the tests in this change have to go through the whole command to check --format and --since validation. Extracting a parseExportOptions(args) that returns the options or a usage error would leave the command as a short orchestration.
